drug_class: Orexin receptor antagonist (dual orexin receptor antagonist)
purpose: Lemborexant is used to help adults who have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, a condition called insomnia. It helps you get to sleep faster and stay asleep longer so you feel more rested. It is meant to be used on nights when you have at least 7 hours before you need to wake up.
how_it_works: Your brain has natural chemicals called orexins that keep you awake and alert. Lemborexant works by blocking the signals from these wake-promoting chemicals, essentially telling your brain it is time to sleep. This helps your brain shift into sleep mode more naturally, rather than just sedating your whole brain.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is feeling sleepy or drowsy the next morning, which can affect your ability to drive or operate machinery. You may also experience unusual or vivid dreams, headache, or dizziness. Some people feel temporarily unable to move or speak when falling asleep or waking up, which is called sleep paralysis.
warnings: Do not drive or do anything that requires full alertness the morning after taking lemborexant, especially at first, as it can cause next-day drowsiness. It can cause complex sleep behaviors like sleepwalking or sleep-driving, so stop taking it and call your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. It is not recommended if you have narcolepsy. It can be habit-forming, so only take it as prescribed and do not share it with others.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken by mouth once per night, right before bedtime, when you have at least 7 hours left for sleep. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg per night if needed. Never take more than one dose per night. Swallow it whole and do not take it with or right after a high-fat, heavy meal, as this can slow how quickly it works.
